sections.h2: What should a Wilkinson County owner know about property tax before selling?
sections.html:
Wilkinson County splits the job between two desks in Irwinton. Assessors put a number on the property. The tax commissioner mails the statement and takes payment. The state revenue department's FAQ is blunt on timing: the person on title each January 1 owes the year, and a spring closing earns no rebate.

The county spreads across 452 square miles near the fall line, where the upper coastal plain starts to roll. Irwinton is the seat, Gordon is the biggest town, and Allentown, Danville, Ivey, McIntyre and Toomsboro complete the list of municipalities. The county dates to May 11, 1803.

The population has drifted down from 10,368 in 1980 to 8,877 in 2020, and an estimate for July 2025 puts it at 8,650. All of the residents counted in 2020 lived in rural areas, at roughly 20 people per square mile. A buyer pool this small makes a clean tax record more valuable.

Gather these before talking to any buyer:

  • last year's bill and the newest assessment notice
  • a note of whether the parcel has a homestead exemption on file
  • the location permit and tax receipt for any manufactured home on the land
  • any letter from the commissioner about overdue balances

sections.h2: Which Wilkinson County office handles which task?
sections.html:
Match the question to the desk and the visit goes quickly.

  • Tax Commissioner at 100 Bacon St., Suite 136, open 8:00 a.m. until 4:45 p.m. Phone (478) 946-2232, fax (478) 946-1429, postal box P.O. Box 182. Online payments add a convenience fee.
  • Board of Assessors and Chief Appraiser, P.O. Box 189, phone (478) 946-2076. This office keeps the tax maps, the ownership transfers, and the records for mobile homes without a homestead. It meets the first Wednesday of the month at 9:30 in the courthouse.
  • Board of Equalization, whose members the grand jury appoints. Each member completes 40 hours of training in the first year and eight hours yearly after that. The Clerk of Superior Court supplies clerical help only.
  • Commissioners and school board, the two bodies that set the rates.

The county website, wilkinsoncounty.net, links to a property record search and posts the current digest with a five-year levy history.

sections.h2: What millage rates apply in Wilkinson County?
sections.html:
Your rate depends on the jurisdiction, since municipal levies sit on top of the county, state and school pieces. The assessors post these 2025 combined totals.

Combined 2025 millage in Wilkinson County, county and city levels, from the assessors' posted list
JurisdictionCombined millage
Unincorporated county32.082

Danville32.082

Irwinton37.892

McIntyre35.302

A mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value. Assessed value is 40% of fair market value, as the commissioner's site spells out.

The county government's own share changed for 2024. A notice from the Board of Commissioners said it would cut its levy from 14.344 to 13.786 mills, which stayed above the 13.227 rollback figure. Staying above rollback required three public hearings, scheduled for January 21 and January 30, 2025 at the courthouse on Bacon Street.

sections.h2: When do Wilkinson County property taxes come due?
sections.html:
The commissioner's page says December 20 is the usual deadline. Your own bill carries the controlling date. The Revenue Department notes that a county may substitute December 1, November 15, or several installments.

No interest accrues for the first 60 days after the postmark on your bill. Penalties may follow later, so get the office's current charges in writing with your payoff.

  • Returns come in between New Year's Day and April 1.
  • A real property return renews itself at the previous value each year, so new filings are needed only when you add structures or buy more land.
  • Ignored bills can lead to a levy against the parcel and a forced sale.

sections.h2: How can I challenge a Wilkinson County valuation?
sections.html:
An appeal goes to the assessors in writing, and the postmark has to land inside a 45-day span that opens when the notice is sent. Disputes can cover what the property is worth, how it compares with neighbors, whether it is taxable, or an exemption you were refused.

On the state form you name your forum: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. Revenue department staff have no power to overturn any of those rulings on one house.

A second entry point is the annual return. Declaring a different value on a return filed by April 1 opens an appeal if the assessors reject your figure. Bring recent sales of similar houses nearby, photographs of defects, and contractor estimates. With homes valued at a median $86,300 here, a few thousand dollars of correction can matter, so documented condition problems are worth the effort.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption work here?
sections.html:
The exemption trims the assessed value of the house you occupy as your main residence. The state default is $2,000, and a county may offer more through local legislation. For Wilkinson County, the assessors' page says the Chief Appraiser takes homestead applications.

File whenever you like. A form arriving after April 1 waits for next year. An owner who never files is treated as having waived it.

A buyer needs a fresh application of their own. If you moved out and rented the house, ask the Chief Appraiser how the parcel is classified.

sections.h2: What if back taxes or a lien show up before the sale?
sections.html:
Your title company asks the commissioner for a payoff figure and deducts it from your proceeds. If a FiFa lien was filed, it appears on the Clerk of Superior Court's execution docket until the tax, fees and interest clear.

Write the proration into the contract, since the county bills one owner of record and never divides a year.

Manufactured homes have extra steps. Revenue department guidance gives the owner 30 days after placement to obtain a location permit, then a yearly renewal each winter, plus a return due April 1. Check that all three are current before you advertise.

sections.h2: What do local housing numbers look like in Wilkinson County?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists a $86,300 median home value for the 2020 to 2024 period, and owners occupy 80.5% of houses. The decennial count in 2020 found 3,588 households and 4,288 housing units, with 16.3% of units vacant. Rent runs a median $825 a month. Owners with a mortgage report $1,037 in monthly costs, against $446 for owners who are debt-free.

Median household income is $45,465 and per capita income is $25,403. Residents had a median age of 44.9 in 2020, and 20.4% had reached 65. A bachelor's degree is held by 12.3% of adults, and 78.5% of households subscribe to broadband.

The county counted 143 employer establishments with 2,543 jobs in 2023, and 18 building permits in 2025. Workers spend an average of 26.9 minutes getting to their jobs. Wilkinson County School District is the sole public district. The county's neighbors are Baldwin, Bleckley, Washington, Johnson, Laurens, Twiggs and Jones.

faqs.q: Who mails the property tax statement in Wilkinson County?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner does. The office is on Bacon Street in Irwinton and answers at (478) 946-2232. Value disputes belong to the assessors at (478) 946-2076.

faqs.q: Is December 20 the due date for Wilkinson County taxes?
faqs.a: Usually, as the commissioner's website puts it. Follow the date on your own bill, because a county can pick an earlier deadline.

faqs.q: What is the window for contesting a Wilkinson County value?
faqs.a: The count of 45 days starts when the notice is sent. Address the written appeal to the assessors at P.O. Box 189.

faqs.q: Does a mid-year sale shift the tax to the buyer?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The owner on New Year's Day is on the hook for twelve months, so sellers and buyers usually divide the bill inside the contract.

faqs.q: Where is the homestead exemption filed in Wilkinson County?
faqs.a: At the assessors' office, where the Chief Appraiser takes applications.
